title: Windows Server: instalación de roles + features
tags: windows server, role, feature, install, servermanager
excerpt: Cómo agregar/quitar roles + features de forma sistemática.
body:
## Métodos
### 1. Server Manager (GUI)
- `Manage → Add Roles and Features`
- Wizard step-by-step
- Descripciones + dependencies

### 2. PowerShell (recomendado enterprise)
```powershell
# Ver todos los roles/features + estado
Get-WindowsFeature

# Filtrar solo instalados
Get-WindowsFeature | Where-Object InstallState -eq Installed

# Buscar
Get-WindowsFeature *IIS*

# Instalar
Install-WindowsFeature -Name Web-Server -IncludeManagementTools -IncludeAllSubFeature

# Uninstall
Uninstall-WindowsFeature -Name Web-Server -Remove

# Config file (declarativo)
Install-WindowsFeature -ConfigurationFilePath 'C:\config.xml'
```

### 3. DISM (offline images)
```powershell
DISM /Online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:IIS-WebServer /All
DISM /Online /Get-Features   # lista
```

## Roles comunes

### AD DS (Active Directory Domain Services)
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature AD-Domain-Services -IncludeManagementTools
# Después promocionar como DC:
Install-ADDSForest -DomainName 'empresa.local' -InstallDNS
```

### IIS
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature Web-Server -IncludeManagementTools -IncludeAllSubFeature
```

### DNS
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature DNS -IncludeManagementTools
```

### DHCP
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature DHCP -IncludeManagementTools
```

### Hyper-V
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature Hyper-V -IncludeManagementTools -Restart
```
Requires CPU virtualization + reboot.

### File Server + Deduplication
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature File-Services, FS-Data-Deduplication -IncludeManagementTools
```

### Failover Clustering
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature Failover-Clustering -IncludeManagementTools
```

### Print + Document Services
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature Print-Server, Print-LPD-Service -IncludeManagementTools
```

### Remote Desktop Services (RDS)
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature RDS-RD-Server, RDS-Licensing, RDS-Web-Access -IncludeManagementTools
```

### Certificate Services (AD CS)
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature ADCS-Cert-Authority -IncludeManagementTools
Install-AdcsCertificationAuthority -CAType EnterpriseRootCA
```

## Features útiles

### .NET Framework
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature NET-Framework-45-Features
Install-WindowsFeature NET-Framework-Core   # 3.5 legacy
```

### Windows Backup
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature Windows-Server-Backup
```

### PowerShell 2.0 engine (legacy compat)
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature PowerShell-V2
```

### RSAT (Remote Server Administration Tools)
Para managing otros servers desde este:
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature RSAT-AD-Tools, RSAT-DNS-Server, RSAT-DHCP -IncludeAllSubFeature
```

## Server Core
Windows Server sin GUI (headless):
- Menor footprint
- Menos parches (menor ataque)
- Solo PowerShell + sconfig

### Cambiar entre Server Core y GUI
Desktop Experience feature:
```powershell
# Add GUI
Install-WindowsFeature Server-Gui-Mgmt-Infra, Server-Gui-Shell -Restart

# Remove GUI (back a Core)
Uninstall-WindowsFeature Server-Gui-Mgmt-Infra, Server-Gui-Shell -Restart
```

Nota: Server 2022+ no permite añadir GUI si install fue Core. Reinstall required.

## Feature Windows Container / Docker
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature Containers -Restart
# Instalar Docker
Install-Module DockerMsftProvider
Install-Package Docker -ProviderName DockerMsftProvider -Force
```

## Best practices

### 1. Principle of least install
Solo instalar features estrictamente necesarios. Menos surface para vulnerabilidades.

### 2. Config as code
Generar config XML:
```powershell
Get-WindowsFeature | Where InstallState -eq Installed |
    Export-Csv -Path C:\features.csv
```

Replicar en otros servers.

### 3. DSC (Desired State Configuration)
PowerShell DSC declara state deseado:
```powershell
Configuration WebServer {
    Node 'localhost' {
        WindowsFeature IIS {
            Ensure = 'Present'
            Name = 'Web-Server'
            IncludeAllSubFeature = $true
        }
    }
}
WebServer
Start-DscConfiguration -Path .\WebServer -Wait -Verbose
```

### 4. Documentar
Cada server tiene inventory de roles instalados.

### 5. Test en QA
Instalar features en QA + verificar antes de PRD.

### 6. Reboot planeados
Algunos features requieren reboot. Coordinar con business.

## Common issues

### 'Feature no está en la lista'
- Media source needed (feature no en Windows por default)
- `Install-WindowsFeature -Source \\file-server\wim`

### 'Error 0x800F0906' — source files
Windows Update no puede resolver dependency. Provide source path.

### 'Reboot required loop'
Algunos features tras install piden reboot. Después de reboot completar.

### 'Feature blocked por policy'
SCCM/GPO puede bloquear installations. Consultar admin.

## Ver estado post-install
```powershell
Get-Service                        # servicios corriendo
Get-WindowsFeature | Where InstallState -eq Installed
```

## Automation
Ansible / Chef / Puppet manage Windows Server también:
```yaml
# Ansible
- name: Install IIS
  win_feature:
    name: Web-Server
    include_management_tools: yes
    include_sub_features: yes
```

## Autorización
- Local Administrator o Domain Admin
- Delegated permissions con RBAC (JEA)

title: Windows Server: IIS avanzado — application pools, bindings, modules
tags: iis, windows server, web, application pool, binding
excerpt: Config avanzada de IIS: pools, bindings, autenticación, deploy.
body:
## Application pools
Pool = process isolation entre sites/apps.

### Configurar pool
```powershell
Import-Module WebAdministration

# Crear pool
New-WebAppPool -Name 'MyAppPool'

# Config
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\AppPools\MyAppPool' processModel.identityType 'ApplicationPoolIdentity'
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\AppPools\MyAppPool' recycling.periodicRestart.time '00:00:00'  # never
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\AppPools\MyAppPool' recycling.periodicRestart.schedule.[value='03:00:00'] '03:00:00'  # daily 3AM
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\AppPools\MyAppPool' processModel.idleTimeout '00:00:00'  # never idle timeout
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\AppPools\MyAppPool' managedRuntimeVersion 'v4.0'
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\AppPools\MyAppPool' enable32BitAppOnWin64 $false
```

### Identity options
- **ApplicationPoolIdentity** (default) — auto-generated `IIS APPPOOL\MyAppPool` user
- **LocalService** — limited system account
- **LocalSystem** — full system access (peligroso)
- **NetworkService** — network-authenticated
- **SpecificUser** — dominio\svc_web con password

**Recomendado**: ApplicationPoolIdentity con NTFS permissions específicos.

### Recycling
- **Idle timeout**: 20 min default (app se suspende). Change to `00:00:00` para keep-alive.
- **Periodic restart**: cada 1740 min (29h) default. Change a specific time o disable.
- **Regular time interval**: cada N minutes
- **Specific time**: solo a HH:MM

Recycles gracefully — evita memory leaks.

## Bindings
Qué IPs/puertos/hostnames listens el site.

### Config vía UI
IIS Manager → site → **Bindings**:
- Type: http o https
- IP: All Unassigned o specific
- Port: 80/443 (o custom)
- Host name: `www.empresa.com` (SNI)
- SSL Cert (para HTTPS)

### PowerShell
```powershell
New-WebBinding -Name 'MySite' -Protocol http -HostHeader 'www.empresa.com' -Port 80
New-WebBinding -Name 'MySite' -Protocol https -HostHeader 'www.empresa.com' -Port 443 -SslFlags 1  # SNI
```

### SNI (Server Name Indication)
HTTPS bindings para multiple sites en mismo IP:
- Sin SNI: 1 cert por IP
- Con SNI: multiple certs, discriminados por hostname

## Certificados HTTPS

### Import cert
```powershell
Import-PfxCertificate -FilePath 'C:\cert.pfx' -CertStoreLocation Cert:\LocalMachine\My -Password (ConvertTo-SecureString 'pfxpassword' -AsPlainText -Force)
```

### Bind cert al site
```powershell
$cert = Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where Subject -like '*CN=www.empresa.com*'
$binding = Get-WebBinding -Name 'MySite' -Protocol https
$binding.AddSslCertificate($cert.Thumbprint, 'my')
```

### Renovar
Generate CSR desde IIS → send to CA → import back → rebind.

Or use Let's Encrypt con win-acme (Certify):
```powershell
Install-Module Certify
Start-Certify
```

## Authentication

### Anonymous (default)
Cualquiera puede acceder.

### Windows Authentication
Integrated con AD:
- User logged in Windows auto-auth
- Ideal intranet

### Basic
User + password (base64). Requires HTTPS.

### Forms
Custom login page.

### Client Certificate
mTLS.

### Config
```powershell
Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'IIS:\Sites\MySite' -Filter 'system.webServer/security/authentication/anonymousAuthentication' -Name enabled -Value $false
Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'IIS:\Sites\MySite' -Filter 'system.webServer/security/authentication/windowsAuthentication' -Name enabled -Value $true
```

## URL Rewrite
Download plugin: https://iis.net/downloads/microsoft/url-rewrite

Rules en web.config:
```xml
<rewrite>
    <rules>
        <rule name='HTTP to HTTPS' stopProcessing='true'>
            <match url='(.*)' />
            <conditions>
                <add input='{HTTPS}' pattern='off' />
            </conditions>
            <action type='Redirect' url='https://{HTTP_HOST}/{R:1}' />
        </rule>
    </rules>
</rewrite>
```

## Application Request Routing (ARR)
Reverse proxy load balancing:
- Fronts multiple backend servers
- Health checks
- Session affinity

Download: https://iis.net/downloads/microsoft/application-request-routing

## Compression
```xml
<system.webServer>
    <httpCompression>
        <staticTypes>
            <add mimeType='text/*' enabled='true' />
            <add mimeType='application/javascript' enabled='true' />
        </staticTypes>
    </httpCompression>
</system.webServer>
```

## HTTPS security headers
```xml
<system.webServer>
    <httpProtocol>
        <customHeaders>
            <add name='Strict-Transport-Security' value='max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains' />
            <add name='X-Content-Type-Options' value='nosniff' />
            <add name='X-Frame-Options' value='SAMEORIGIN' />
            <add name='Referrer-Policy' value='strict-origin-when-cross-origin' />
        </customHeaders>
    </httpProtocol>
</system.webServer>
```

## Logs
Location: `%SystemDrive%\inetpub\logs\LogFiles\W3SVC<siteId>\`

Format: W3C (default) — parseable con Log Parser / Splunk.

Rotate: daily automáticamente. Delete old:
```powershell
Get-ChildItem 'C:\inetpub\logs\LogFiles' -Recurse -File | 
    Where LastWriteTime -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-30) | 
    Remove-Item
```

## Monitoring

### Perfmon counters
- `Web Service(_Total)\Current Connections`
- `Web Service(_Total)\Bytes Total/sec`
- `ASP.NET Applications(_Total)\Requests/Sec`
- `Process(w3wp)\% Processor Time`
- `Process(w3wp)\Working Set`

### Failed Request Tracing
Granular debugging:
1. IIS Manager → site → **Failed Request Tracing Rules**
2. Enable + config para status codes específicos (500, timeouts)
3. Files generados en `C:\inetpub\logs\FailedReqLogFiles\`

## Deploy

### MSDeploy (Web Deploy)
```powershell
Install-Module IISAdministration  # o MSDeploy tool download

msdeploy -verb:sync -source:package='C:\build.zip' -dest:auto,computerName='https://server:8172/msdeploy.axd?site=MySite',authType='Basic',userName='...',password='...'
```

### Manual
- Copy files a `C:\inetpub\wwwroot\MySite\`
- Restart pool: `Restart-WebAppPool 'MyAppPool'`

## Common issues

### 'HTTP 503 Service Unavailable'
- Application pool stopped o crashed
- `Get-WebAppPoolState 'MyAppPool'` — if Stopped → `Start-WebAppPool 'MyAppPool'`
- Ver Event Viewer para crash reason

### 'HTTP 500.19 — invalid config'
Detail cubierto en artículo IIS 500.19 específico.

### 'Site starts but returns 500'
- Application error
- Enable detailed errors localmente (nunca en prod):
```xml
<httpErrors errorMode='Detailed' />
```
- Check Windows event log Application

### 'Slow response'
- Check w3wp CPU/memory
- Perfmon en cuenta
- Add more pool workers si CPU-bound
- Debugger attached puede ralentizar

## Best practices
- **Application pool per site** — isolation
- **HTTPS only** con HSTS
- **Security headers** configurados
- **Logs a SIEM** — audit + performance
- **Recycling appropriate** — memory leaks mitigated
- **Deploy via CI/CD** — no manual copies
- **Backup web.config** antes de cambios

## Autorización
- Local Administrator para config
- Delegated auth via IIS Manager users si multi-tenant

title: Windows Server: Active Directory sites + replication
tags: ad, active directory, replication, site, subnet
excerpt: AD Sites, subnets, replication topology + troubleshooting.
body:
## AD Sites
Containers lógicos que representan ubicaciones físicas (datacenters, oficinas).

### Por qué
- **Optimize replication traffic** — DCs replican dentro de site rápido, entre sites lento (según schedule)
- **Client localization** — client busca DC en su site primero (locality)
- **Service localization** — Exchange, Certificate Services encuentran nearest server

## Componentes

### Site
Contenedor con:
- DCs
- Subnets asociadas
- Site Links (con otros sites)

### Subnet
CIDR range mapped a site:
- `10.10.0.0/16` → Site 'Bogota'
- `10.20.0.0/16` → Site 'Mexico'

Client con IP en subnet → knows su site → busca DC allí.

### Site Link
Conexión virtual entre 2+ sites:
- Cost (bandwidth relative)
- Schedule (cuándo replica)
- Interval (frecuencia)

## Manage via GUI
`Active Directory Sites and Services` (`dssite.msc`).

### Add site
Right-click **Sites** → **New Site** → name (ej: 'Bogota') → site link (default `DEFAULTIPSITELINK`).

### Add subnet
Right-click **Subnets** → **New Subnet**:
- Prefix: `10.10.0.0/16`
- Site: Bogota

### Move DC to site
Sites → drag DC entre sites.

## PowerShell
```powershell
Import-Module ActiveDirectory

# Ver sites
Get-ADReplicationSite

# Crear site
New-ADReplicationSite -Name 'Bogota'

# Crear subnet
New-ADReplicationSubnet -Name '10.10.0.0/16' -Site 'Bogota'

# Ver DCs por site
Get-ADDomainController -Filter * | Group-Object Site

# Ver site links
Get-ADReplicationSiteLink
```

## Replication topology

### KCC (Knowledge Consistency Checker)
Daemon que corre en cada DC:
- Genera automatically replication connections
- Considera cost + schedule de site links
- Recalculates cada 15 min

### Manual override
En casos edge:
- Sites and Services → **NTDS Settings** → **New Connection** con specific DC

### Force replication
```powershell
repadmin /replicate <DC_target> <DC_source> DC=empresa,DC=local
```

Or GUI: right-click NTDS Settings → **Replicate Now**.

## Bridgehead servers
Per site, un DC actúa como bridgehead — replica con otros sites (los otros DCs del site replican entre sí).

KCC selecciona automáticamente. Manual override en NTDS Settings.

## Site link costs
Default: 100.

Adjust based on bandwidth:
- 1000 (slow WAN link)
- 50 (fast link)
- 10 (fiber/datacenter interconnect)

KCC prefers low-cost links.

## Schedule
Controlar cuándo replica:
- Default: 24/7
- Restringir a off-hours si bandwidth es scarce

Site link → **Change Schedule**.

## Interval
Frequency de replication:
- Default: 180 min (3h)
- Reducir para faster sync: 15 min minimum

## Diagnóstico

### repadmin
Suite de tools de replication:
```powershell
repadmin /showrepl                    # estado en local DC
repadmin /replsummary                 # summary de todos los DCs
repadmin /replsummary /BYSRC /BYDEST  # both directions
repadmin /showrepl <DC>               # remote DC
repadmin /kcc                         # trigger KCC recalc
repadmin /queue                       # replication queue
repadmin /showbackup                  # last backup on each DC
```

### dcdiag
Deep diagnostics:
```powershell
dcdiag /v                             # verbose
dcdiag /test:replications             # solo replication
dcdiag /test:dns                      # DNS checks
```

### Common errors

#### 'DsReplicaSync failed 8453'
User sin auth para replication. Verify user en 'Enterprise Domain Controllers' group.

#### 'DsReplicaSync failed 8524'
DNS issue. Verify SRV records: `_ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.empresa.local`.

#### 'DsBind failed 1722'
RPC blocked. Firewall issue between DCs.

#### 'Time skew > 5 min'
Kerberos requires clock sync:
```powershell
w32tm /query /status
w32tm /resync
```

#### 'USN Journal Wrap'
DC estuvo off long → journal wrapped. Restore desde backup o non-authoritative demote/re-promote.

#### 'Tombstone lifetime exceeded'
DC offline >180 días → cannot rejoin. Rebuild from scratch.

## SYSVOL replication
Aparte del DIT replication:

### FRS (legacy — deprecated)
### DFSR (moderno)

Ambos replican SYSVOL folder ($SystemRoot%\SYSVOL).

### Verificar DFSR
```powershell
dfsrmig /getglobalstate
# Debería ser 'ELIMINATED' (fully migrated to DFSR)
```

### Backlog
```powershell
dfsrdiag Backlog /RGName:'Domain System Volume' /RFName:'SYSVOL Share' /SMem:DC1 /RMem:DC2
```

## FSMO roles
5 Flexible Single Master Operations:
- **Schema Master** (forest-wide)
- **Domain Naming Master** (forest-wide)
- **RID Master** (domain-wide)
- **PDC Emulator** (domain-wide) — critical, does password chain, time source
- **Infrastructure Master** (domain-wide)

### Ver
```powershell
netdom query fsmo
```

### Transfer
```powershell
Move-ADDirectoryServerOperationMasterRole -Identity 'DC2' -OperationMasterRole PDCEmulator
```

### Seize (si DC dueño down)
```powershell
Move-ADDirectoryServerOperationMasterRole -Identity 'DC2' -OperationMasterRole PDCEmulator -Force
```

Peligroso — asegurate que original DC está permanentemente down.

## Best practices
- **Sites reflect physical topology** — no over-engineer
- **Subnets always defined** — clients sin subnet → default site (bad)
- **At least 2 DCs per site** para HA
- **KCC auto** — resist manual connections
- **Monitor replication** — dcdiag semanal + repadmin diario
- **Backup DIT regularly** — Windows Server Backup
- **Time sync** critical — NTP hierarchy PDC-out

## Autorización
- Domain Admins para modify sites
- Enterprise Admins para forest-wide changes
- Delegated permissions con OU-specific admins

title: Windows Server: Group Policy design + troubleshooting
tags: gpo, group policy, gpupdate, rsop, gpresult
excerpt: Design de GPOs a escala + troubleshooting.
body:
## GPO overview
Centraliza config de Windows machines + users:
- Password policies
- Software deployment
- Login scripts
- Drive mappings
- Firewall rules
- Etc.

## Estructura

### Scope de un GPO
- **Local** — en cada machine (gpedit.msc)
- **Site** — todos los DCs del site
- **Domain** — todo el domain
- **OU** — específica organizational unit

Orden de aplicación: **L**ocal → **S**ite → **D**omain → **O**U (LSDO).

Última gana (OU override domain, etc.).

### Order dentro de scope
Multiple GPOs en same OU:
- 'Enforced' GPOs always win
- Otherwise: link order (higher number = lower priority)

## Crear GPO

### GPMC (`gpmc.msc`)
1. Group Policy Objects → right-click → **New**
2. Name: `Z_Corp_Firewall_Rules`
3. Right-click new GPO → **Edit**
4. GPME opens

### Link a OU
Right-click OU → **Link an Existing GPO**.

## Common settings

### Password policy (domain root only)
**Computer Config → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Account Policies → Password Policy**:
- Min length: 12
- Complexity: enabled
- History: 24
- Max age: 90
- Min age: 1

### Screensaver password
**User Config → Admin Templates → Control Panel → Personalization**:
- Password protect the screen saver: Enabled
- Screen saver timeout: 900 sec (15 min)

### Software install
**User (o Computer) Config → Software Settings → Software Installation**:
- New Package (MSI)
- Assigned or Published

### Login script
**User Config → Windows Settings → Scripts → Logon**:
- Add script
- Params

### Drive mapping
**User Config → Preferences → Windows Settings → Drive Maps**:
- Path: `\\fileserver\shared`
- Drive letter: Z:
- Reconnect: yes
- Item-level targeting: group `Sales`

### Firewall rules
**Computer Config → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security**

## Troubleshooting

### gpupdate
Force policy refresh:
```powershell
gpupdate /force               # apply immediately
gpupdate /force /boot         # requires reboot
gpupdate /force /logoff       # requires logoff
```

Default refresh: cada 90 min + 30 min random.

### gpresult
Ver qué policies apply al user/machine:
```powershell
gpresult /r                   # resumen
gpresult /r /scope user
gpresult /r /scope computer
gpresult /h C:\report.html    # HTML report full
invoke-item C:\report.html
```

### RSoP (Resultant Set of Policy)
```powershell
rsop.msc
```

GUI mostrando qué se aplicó.

### Modeling (predictive)
GPMC → **Group Policy Modeling** → **Group Policy Modeling Wizard** → simula:
- User X en OU Y en Site Z → qué GPOs se aplicarán

Útil antes de aplicar cambios.

### Results (real actual)
GPMC → **Group Policy Results** → wizard connecting to real machine → snapshot de policies applied.

## Cuándo policies no aplican

### 1. Wrong scope
GPO linked a OU incorrecta. User no está en esa OU.

**Fix**: Move user to correct OU o re-link GPO.

### 2. Security filtering
GPO → tab **Scope** → **Security Filtering**:
- Default: 'Authenticated Users'
- If replaced with specific group, user must be member

**Fix**: add user to group o restore Authenticated Users.

### 3. WMI filter
GPO → **WMI Filtering**:
- Query WMI que debe return true para que GPO apply
- Ejemplo: `SELECT * FROM Win32_OperatingSystem WHERE Version LIKE '10.%'` (only Windows 10)

**Fix**: verify WMI query returns expected result.

### 4. Block Inheritance
OU con **Block Inheritance** — GPOs de OU padre NO se aplican.

**Fix**:
- **Enforced** en GPO padre override el block
- O disable block

### 5. Slow link
Some policies solo apply en fast connections:
- **Group Policy → 'Configure Group Policy slow link detection'**

### 6. Client-Side Extension (CSE) disabled
Algunas GPO CSEs pueden estar disabled en el client.

**Fix**: verify service Group Policy Client running.

## Event logs
**Applications and Services Logs → Microsoft → Windows → GroupPolicy → Operational**:
- Event 4001 — starting processing
- Event 4016 — CSE processing (con tiempo)
- Event 5017 — network issue

Critical para debugging.

## Loopback processing
Users en machines especiales (kiosks, RDS):
- User config normalmente aplica según OU del user
- Con loopback: user config aplica según OU de la machine

### Enable
**Computer Config → Admin Templates → System → Group Policy → 'User Group Policy loopback processing mode'**:
- **Merge** — user's normal + machine's loopback
- **Replace** — only machine's loopback (usa case kiosco)

## Central Store
ADMX/ADML templates centralizados en SYSVOL:
- `\\empresa.local\SYSVOL\empresa.local\Policies\PolicyDefinitions`

Once configured, all admins ven mismos templates.

### Setup
```powershell
robocopy C:\Windows\PolicyDefinitions \\empresa.local\SYSVOL\empresa.local\Policies\PolicyDefinitions /E
```

## Best practices

### 1. Naming convention
`Z_<Purpose>_<Scope>` — ej: `Z_Firewall_Servers`, `Z_Drives_Sales`.

### 2. Small GPOs
No mega-GPOs con hundreds settings. Split por functional area.

### 3. OU structure alineada
OUs = departments (usually). GPOs = purpose. Link GPOs a OUs relevantes.

### 4. Documentation
Cada GPO tiene comment (description) explicando purpose + owner.

### 5. Change management
GPO changes con CAB approval (like ITIL change management).

### 6. Backup GPOs regularmente
```powershell
Backup-GPO -All -Path 'C:\GPO-Backups\' -Comment 'Weekly backup'
```

### 7. Test antes de PRD
- Modeling first
- Deploy a Test OU
- Verify
- Move to Production

### 8. Item-level targeting
En Preferences: targetear granularmente sin fragmentar GPOs.

## GPO ADMX custom
Si tercer party (ej: Chrome, Firefox, Office) provee ADMX:
1. Download ADMX + ADML
2. Copy a Central Store
3. Aparece automatically en GPME

## PowerShell alternative
Algunos settings mejor con DSC (Desired State Configuration) o Intune (cloud).

## Common issues

### 'gpupdate hangs'
- Network to DC issue
- SYSVOL replication broken
- Ver Event Viewer GroupPolicy/Operational

### 'Setting shows en RSoP pero no efectivo'
- Cache issue → reboot
- CSE not installed en client
- Ver client-side logs

### 'New setting takes forever'
Default refresh 90 min. Forzar con gpupdate.

## Autorización
- Domain Admins para modify GPOs
- Delegated GPO permissions via Group Policy Creator Owners

title: Windows Server: Failover Clustering — HA para servicios
tags: cluster, failover, ha, quorum, csv, windows server
excerpt: Setup + operación de Windows Failover Cluster.
body:
## Failover Cluster
HA feature de Windows Server:
- Group de servers (nodes) que actúan como unidad
- Si un node falla, otro toma over automáticamente
- Usado para SQL Server AGs, Hyper-V, File Server, Exchange

## Requerimientos
- **Windows Server 2019/2022 Standard o Datacenter**
- Nodes en **mismo dominio AD**
- Shared storage (para roles que lo requieren):
  - iSCSI SAN
  - Fibre Channel SAN
  - SMB share
  - Storage Spaces Direct (S2D)
- Network:
  - Client access LAN
  - Cluster heartbeat network (isolated, redundant)

## Install
```powershell
# En cada node
Install-WindowsFeature Failover-Clustering -IncludeManagementTools
```

## Validation
Antes de crear cluster, validar setup:

```powershell
Test-Cluster -Node node1, node2, node3
```

O GUI: Failover Cluster Manager → **Validate Configuration**.

Genera report HTML con:
- ✅ Cluster capable
- ⚠️ Warnings (recomendaciones)
- ❌ Errors (must fix before create)

## Crear cluster
```powershell
New-Cluster -Name 'ClusterA' -Node node1, node2, node3 -StaticAddress 10.0.0.100 -NoStorage
```

- `-StaticAddress`: cluster IP (VIP)
- `-NoStorage`: no auto-add shared disks (add later)

## Quorum
Algoritmo que decide 'who owns the cluster':
- Evitar split-brain (2 nodes think they're master)
- Majority vote

### Modes
- **Node Majority** — cada node vota. Best con 3+ nodes odd
- **Node and Disk Majority** — nodes + disk witness (2-node clusters)
- **Node and File Share Majority** — nodes + SMB share
- **Cloud Witness** (2016+) — Azure Storage account
- **Disk Only** — legacy

### Config Cloud Witness
```powershell
Set-ClusterQuorum -CloudWitness -AccountName 'myAzureStorage' -AccessKey '<key>'
```

Con 2 nodes + cloud witness: HA sin third node físico.

## Shared storage

### iSCSI target (para test/small)
```powershell
# On file server (o dedicado)
Install-WindowsFeature FS-iSCSITarget-Server -IncludeManagementTools
New-IscsiVirtualDisk -Path 'D:\iSCSI\quorum.vhdx' -Size 1GB
New-IscsiVirtualDisk -Path 'D:\iSCSI\csv1.vhdx' -Size 500GB
New-IscsiServerTarget -TargetName 'cluster-target' -InitiatorIds 'IQN:iqn.1991-05.com.microsoft:node1.empresa.local','IQN:iqn.1991-05.com.microsoft:node2.empresa.local'
Add-IscsiVirtualDiskTargetMapping -TargetName 'cluster-target' -DevicePath 'D:\iSCSI\quorum.vhdx'
Add-IscsiVirtualDiskTargetMapping -TargetName 'cluster-target' -DevicePath 'D:\iSCSI\csv1.vhdx'
```

Cada node connecta al iSCSI target y ve los disks como si fueran locales.

### Add shared disk al cluster
```powershell
Get-ClusterAvailableDisk | Add-ClusterDisk
```

### Cluster Shared Volume (CSV)
Disks accesibles concurrentemente por múltiples nodes (para Hyper-V, S2D):
```powershell
Get-ClusterResource | Where { $_.ResourceType -eq 'Physical Disk' -and $_.State -eq 'Online' } |
    Add-ClusterSharedVolume
```

CSVs aparecen como `C:\ClusterStorage\Volume1`, `Volume2`, etc.

## Roles / apps clusterizables

### File Server
```powershell
Add-ClusterFileServerRole -Storage 'Cluster Disk 1' -Name 'ClusterFS'
```

Un node hostea el file server. Si falla, otro toma over.

### SQL Server
AOAG (Always On Availability Group) — modern approach:
- Cada node tiene copia
- Sync o async replication
- Failover automático

O Failover Cluster Instance (FCI) — legacy, requires shared disk.

### Hyper-V
VMs corren en CSV. HA + live migration disponibles.

### DHCP, DNS, Print
Algunos servicios menos usan cluster (SCVMM en su lugar).

## Operations

### Ver estado
```powershell
Get-ClusterNode                                # nodes + estado
Get-ClusterGroup                               # roles + owner node
Get-ClusterResource                            # resources con state
Get-ClusterSharedVolume
Get-ClusterNetwork
```

### Failover manual
```powershell
Move-ClusterGroup -Name 'ClusterFS' -Node node2
```

Role se mueve a node2. Test failover.

### Pause/drain node
Before maintenance:
```powershell
Suspend-ClusterNode -Name node1 -Drain
```

Roles moved to other nodes. Node ready for updates.

### Resume
```powershell
Resume-ClusterNode -Name node1
```

### Restart node
Drain first, restart, resume.

## Storage Spaces Direct (S2D)
Modern hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI):
- No shared storage
- Cada node tiene local SSD/NVMe
- Software pools + mirrors data across nodes

### Enable
```powershell
Enable-ClusterS2D -Autoconfig $true
```

Cluster con S2D = mini-SAN. Ideal para 3-16 nodes.

## Monitoring

### Failover Cluster Manager
GUI moderno. Ver dashboard, events, resources.

### Windows Admin Center
Web-based, superior UX. Recomendado.

### Perfmon counters
- Cluster CSV File System
- Cluster Networks

### Alertas
Windows Admin Center o SCVMM tiene alerts nativos.

## Common issues

### 'Node cannot join cluster'
- Not en domain
- Firewall blocking cluster communication (need to allow Failover Clustering rule group)
- Network heartbeat not reachable
- Wrong OS version

### 'Quorum lost'
Multiple nodes fail simultáneo:
```powershell
Start-Cluster -Force -Confirm:$false
```

Force start con reducido quorum.

### 'Split brain'
2 groups of nodes think they own cluster. Rare with proper quorum.

**Fix**: verify quorum config, network isolation.

### 'Role failing to start'
- Ver dependencies (`Get-ClusterResourceDependency`)
- Ver events per resource
- Physical disk issue underlying

### 'Slow failover'
- Networks not sized properly
- Heartbeat sur network con user traffic
- Storage latency

## Best practices

### 1. Dedicated networks
- Client access
- Cluster heartbeat (isolated, redundant)
- Storage (SAN traffic)
- Live Migration (Hyper-V)

### 2. Redundant paths
MPIO for storage, teamed NICs for networks.

### 3. Cloud Witness
Even 2-node cluster: use cloud witness. Simpler than disk witness.

### 4. Regular testing
Manual failover monthly. Verify apps recover.

### 5. Documentation
Runbook per role: recovery steps, dependencies, owners.

### 6. Monitoring
Events to SIEM. Alerts on state changes.

### 7. Patching
- Cluster-Aware Updating (CAU) — orchestrated Windows Update
- Drain-patch-resume por node

## Autorización
- Cluster admins are Domain Admins
- Delegated permissions posible via CNO (Cluster Name Object)

title: Windows Server: WSUS deep — clientes + reports
excerpt: Config avanzada de WSUS + client management.
body:
## WSUS deep dive
Windows Server Update Services — central update repository.

### Beneficios
- Central control de qué updates deploy
- Reduce internet bandwidth (1 download)
- Reporting + compliance

## Setup

### Install
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature UpdateServices, UpdateServices-DB -IncludeManagementTools

# Post-install
& 'C:\Program Files\Update Services\Tools\wsusutil.exe' postinstall CONTENT_DIR=E:\WSUS
```

WSUS almacena patches en `E:\WSUS` (define adequate storage — hundreds GB).

### Configuration wizard
1. `Windows Server Update Services` console
2. **Configuration wizard**:
   - Upstream server: Microsoft Update (o WSUS parent)
   - Proxy (if applicable)
   - Languages: English + Spanish
   - Products: only lo que uses (Windows 10/11, Server 2019/2022, Office, etc.)
   - Classifications: Critical, Security, Definition Updates
   - Sync schedule: daily

### Storage
- Update files: ~200-500 GB for enterprise (grows with time)
- Delete unused: `wsusutil.exe reset` (careful)

## Approve updates

### Manual per group
1. WSUS console → **Updates → Critical Updates** (o category)
2. Right-click update → **Approve**
3. Choose action per computer group:
   - **Install** — deploy
   - **Not approved** — do nothing
   - **Removed** — uninstall

### Auto-approve rules
**Options → Automatic Approvals**:
- New Rule:
  - Classifications: Critical, Security
  - Products: all
  - Groups: 'Servers'
  - Deadline: 7 days

Updates matching rule → auto-approve on sync.

### Compliance report
**Reports → Update Status Summary** → aggregate.

**Computer Status Summary** → per-computer.

## Computer groups
Default:
- **All Computers**
- **Unassigned Computers**

### Custom
Ejemplo por env:
- Test → 10-20 PCs
- Pilot → 50-100 users
- Production → rest

### Assign
**Server-side** (WSUS console): move computer to group.

**Client-side** (GPO target):
- **Computer Config → Admin Templates → Windows Components → Windows Update → 'Enable client-side targeting'**
- Value: name del group (case-sensitive)

## Client config

### GPO
**Windows Update** settings:
- **Configure Automatic Updates**: 4 (auto download and schedule install)
- **Specify intranet Microsoft update service location**:
  - Set the intranet update service: `http://wsus.empresa.local:8530`
  - Set the intranet statistics server: `http://wsus.empresa.local:8530`
- **No auto-restart with logged on users**: enabled (avoid data loss)
- **Scheduled install day**: Every Sunday
- **Scheduled install time**: 03:00

### Registry (per PC)
```
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate
    WUServer = 'http://wsus.empresa.local:8530'
    WUStatusServer = 'http://wsus.empresa.local:8530'
    TargetGroup = 'Production'
    TargetGroupEnabled = 1

HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU
    NoAutoUpdate = 0
    AUOptions = 4
```

## Cliente forza detección
```powershell
# Elder Windows (7, 8, older 10)
wuauclt /detectnow /resetauthorization

# Modern Windows 10/11 (usoclient)
usoclient StartScan
usoclient RefreshSettings

# Or via COM
(New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.AutoUpdate).DetectNow()
```

## Reset client state
Si client stuck o duplicated en WSUS:

```powershell
net stop wuauserv
net stop bits

Remove-ItemProperty HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate -Name AccountDomainSid -Force -EA SilentlyContinue
Remove-ItemProperty HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate -Name PingID -Force -EA SilentlyContinue
Remove-ItemProperty HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate -Name SusClientId -Force -EA SilentlyContinue
Remove-ItemProperty HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate -Name SusClientIdValidation -Force -EA SilentlyContinue

Rename-Item C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old

net start wuauserv
net start bits

wuauclt /resetauthorization /detectnow
```

## SUP (Server Update Package)
### Decline superseded
Old updates superseded por new. Decline saves space:
```powershell
Get-WsusServer | Get-WsusUpdate -Classification All -Approval AnyExceptDeclined | 
    Where {$_.Update.PublicationState -eq 'Published' -and $_.SupersededBy.Count -gt 0} |
    Deny-WsusUpdate
```

### Cleanup wizard
**Options → Server Cleanup Wizard**:
- Unused updates + revisions
- Computers not contacted 30+ days
- Unneeded update files
- Expired updates
- Superseded updates

Run mensual.

## Reports built-in
- Update Status Summary
- Computer Status Summary
- Approval / Detection reports

### Custom via PowerShell
```powershell
# Computers not reporting last 7 days
$wsus = Get-WsusServer
$wsus.GetComputerTargets() | 
    Where LastReportedStatusTime -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-7) |
    Select FullDomainName, LastReportedStatusTime |
    Export-Csv 'not-reporting.csv' -NoTypeInformation
```

### Split-out por importance
```powershell
# Critical updates pending across servers
$wsus.GetComputerTargets() | ForEach-Object {
    $count = ($_ | Get-WsusUpdate -Classification Critical -Approval Approved -Status FailedOrNeeded).Count
    [PSCustomObject]@{Server=$_.FullDomainName; Critical=$count}
} | Sort Critical -Desc
```

## Common issues

### 'Client not reporting'
- GPO not applied — verify `gpresult /r`
- Duplicate SusClientId — reset client
- Firewall block port 8530 (or 8531 for SSL)
- WSUS server DNS not resolving

### 'Approval failed'
Update not synced properly, or content missing. Re-sync WSUS.

### 'WSUS console won't open'
- IIS pool `WsusPool` stopped/crashed
- Restart: `Restart-WebAppPool WsusPool`
- If crashes: increase private memory limit del pool (default 1.8 GB → 4 GB+)

### 'DB WSUS growing huge'
Internal SUSDB (WID or SQL). Backup + shrink periódicamente.

### 'Deadline no aplica'
Misconfig client-side (NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers) block. Adjust.

## Alternative: WUfB (Windows Update for Business)
Cloud-based:
- No servidor WSUS needed
- Config via Intune o GPO
- Deferrals, deadlines, staging rings

Recommended future direction.

## Best practices
- **Test group first** — pilot antes de mass rollout
- **Deadlines strict** — auto-install si user delays
- **Reboot windows** planned
- **Decline superseded** — save space
- **Cleanup mensual**
- **Backup SUSDB** semanal
- **Monitor client reports** — surface non-compliant
- **Auto-approve critical** — no dejar en cola

## Autorización
- Local Administrator del server WSUS
- WSUS Administrators group
- Reporting role (view-only)

title: Windows Server: Storage Spaces + Deduplication
tags: storage spaces, deduplication, refs, ntfs, storage
excerpt: Configurar pools de storage con Storage Spaces + Deduplication.
body:
## Storage Spaces
Software-defined storage en Windows Server:
- Pool multiple physical disks
- Create virtual disks (spaces) con resiliency
- Alternative a hardware RAID

## Setup básico

### 1. Ver discos disponibles
```powershell
Get-PhysicalDisk | Where CanPool -eq $true
```

### 2. Create pool
```powershell
$disks = Get-PhysicalDisk -CanPool $true
New-StoragePool -FriendlyName 'MyPool' -StorageSubSystemFriendlyName 'Windows Storage*' -PhysicalDisks $disks
```

### 3. Create virtual disk
```powershell
New-VirtualDisk -StoragePoolFriendlyName 'MyPool' -FriendlyName 'Data1' -Size 500GB -ResiliencySettingName Mirror -ProvisioningType Fixed
```

### Resiliency levels
- **Simple** — no protection (RAID 0-like, striped)
- **Mirror (2-way)** — 1 copy más (like RAID 1)
- **Mirror (3-way)** — 2 copies más
- **Parity** — like RAID 5 (space-efficient, slower writes)

### 4. Initialize + format
```powershell
Get-VirtualDisk -FriendlyName 'Data1' | Get-Disk | Initialize-Disk -PartitionStyle GPT
Get-VirtualDisk -FriendlyName 'Data1' | Get-Disk | New-Partition -UseMaximumSize -AssignDriveLetter |
    Format-Volume -FileSystem ReFS -NewFileSystemLabel 'Data1' -Confirm:$false
```

## ReFS vs NTFS

### NTFS
- Standard, maduro
- Compatible everywhere
- Deduplication supported
- Compression supported
- File System quotas

### ReFS (Resilient File System)
- Modern, integrity checking (bit rot detection)
- Optimized para large volumes (petabytes)
- Copy-on-write (checkpoints fast)
- Block cloning (VHDX creation instant)
- Better con Storage Spaces Direct (S2D)
- **No** boot volume (siempre NTFS)
- **No** deduplication hasta Server 2019+

### Choose
- **File shares corporativos** → NTFS + Dedup
- **Hyper-V storage** → ReFS (block cloning benefit)
- **Backup targets** → ReFS (integrity streams)
- **Boot** → NTFS obligatorio

## Storage Spaces Direct (S2D)
Hyperconverged infrastructure — Storage Spaces cross-nodes:
- Cada node contribuye local disks
- Software crea pool + resilient volumes
- Failure of node = mirror data en otros nodes

### Requisitos
- 2-16 nodes
- Datacenter edition
- Cache tier (NVMe/SSD)
- Capacity tier (SSD/HDD)
- 10 Gbps+ network

### Enable
```powershell
Enable-ClusterS2D -Autoconfig $true
```

SAP HANA + SQL Server AGs benefit hugely.

## Deduplication
Windows Server feature — reduce disk usage identificando duplicate blocks.

### Install
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature FS-Data-Deduplication
```

### Enable en volumen
```powershell
Enable-DedupVolume -Volume E: -UsageType Default
```

### UsageTypes
- **Default** — general purpose file server
- **HyperV** — para VHDs
- **Backup** — for backups (con large IO scheduling)

### Config threshold
```powershell
Set-DedupVolume -Volume E: -MinimumFileAgeDays 3 -MinimumFileSize 32KB -ExcludeFolder 'E:\NoDedup' -ExcludeFileType 'zip','7z'
```

Solo dedupes files >3 días + >32KB.

### Manual dedup run
```powershell
Start-DedupJob -Volume E: -Type Optimization

# Ver progreso
Get-DedupJob

# Stats
Get-DedupStatus -Volume E:
```

### Schedule
Windows creates dedup schedules automáticamente:
- BackgroundOptimization (weekend)
- PriorityOptimization (idle)

### Ver ahorros
```powershell
Get-DedupStatus | Format-List Volume, UsedSpace, SavedSpace, SavingsRate
```

Ejemplo real:
- Volume 5 TB used → 1.5 TB después dedup
- Savings 70% (típico para VDI VHDs)

## Storage tiers (Storage Spaces)

### 2-tier setup
- Fast SSDs (cache tier)
- Slow HDDs (capacity tier)

### Config
```powershell
# Add pool con both
$ssds = Get-PhysicalDisk -CanPool $true -MediaType SSD
$hdds = Get-PhysicalDisk -CanPool $true -MediaType HDD

New-StoragePool -FriendlyName 'TieredPool' -StorageSubSystemFriendlyName 'Windows Storage*' -PhysicalDisks $ssds+$hdds

$ssdTier = New-StorageTier -StoragePoolFriendlyName 'TieredPool' -FriendlyName SSDTier -MediaType SSD
$hddTier = New-StorageTier -StoragePoolFriendlyName 'TieredPool' -FriendlyName HDDTier -MediaType HDD

New-VirtualDisk -StoragePoolFriendlyName 'TieredPool' -FriendlyName 'TieredData' \
    -StorageTiers $ssdTier, $hddTier \
    -StorageTierSizes 100GB, 500GB \
    -ResiliencySettingName Mirror
```

Frequently-used data → SSD. Cold data → HDD. Auto-tiering runtime.

## Storage Replica
Block-level sync/async replication between servers:
- Server-to-server
- Cluster-to-cluster (DR)
- Stretch cluster (multi-site)

### Enable
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature Storage-Replica -IncludeManagementTools -Restart
```

### Config
```powershell
New-SRPartnership -SourceComputerName primary -SourceRGName 'RG-Primary' -SourceVolumeName 'E:' \
                  -DestinationComputerName secondary -DestinationRGName 'RG-Secondary' -DestinationVolumeName 'E:' \
                  -LogVolumeName 'L:'
```

Async mode default. Sync mode disponible con low latency.

## Backup + restore

### VHDX-based
Storage Spaces VHDX are files — can be copied.

### Windows Server Backup (WSB)
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature Windows-Server-Backup
```

Backup GUI o `wbadmin`:
```powershell
wbadmin start backup -backupTarget:\\backup-server\backup -include:E: -allCritical -quiet
```

### Third-party
Veeam, Commvault, Rubrik para enterprise.

## Common issues

### 'Cannot create pool'
- Discos ya en use
- ClearAll first: `Clear-PhysicalDisk -FriendlyName '...'`

### 'Dedup no progresa'
- Files no idle time enough
- ExcludeFolder capturing wrong path
- Ver `Get-DedupJob` — running?

### 'Volume performance drop'
- Storage Spaces con parity slow para random write
- Consider mirror (faster) o hardware RAID

### 'Space reclamation slow'
Trim/UNMAP command:
```powershell
Optimize-Volume -DriveLetter E -ReTrim -Verbose
```

Restores space en thin-provisioned volumes.

## Best practices

### 1. Right resiliency
- Mirror for performance + safety
- Parity for space efficiency (backup targets)

### 2. Tier appropriate
Hot data en SSD, cold en HDD. Auto-tiering saves cost.

### 3. Dedup on file shares
High ROI. Cold data 30-80% savings typical.

### 4. Monitor disk health
```powershell
Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter
```

Catch failing disks early.

### 5. Backup independent
Storage Spaces resilience ≠ backup. Ransomware encrypts protected data too.

### 6. ReFS for special use cases
- Backup targets
- Hyper-V
- Media stores

### 7. Document config
Size, resiliency, tiers, dedup enabled — for DR restore.

## Autorización
- Local Administrator para create pools
- Storage-specific role delegated con RBAC (JEA)

title: Windows Server: NTFS + share permissions gestión
excerpt: Gestión efectiva de permisos NTFS + share.
body:
## Two layers
Acceso a un file share = intersección de:
1. **Share permissions** (SMB layer)
2. **NTFS permissions** (file system layer)

El **más restrictivo** gana.

Ejemplo:
- Share: Read
- NTFS: Full Control
- Effective: Read (share wins)

## Share permissions

### Types
- **Read** — abrir, listar
- **Change** — read + modify
- **Full Control** — todo, incluidos permission changes

### Config via GUI
Right-click folder → **Properties → Sharing → Advanced Sharing → Permissions**.

### Config via PowerShell
```powershell
Grant-SmbShareAccess -Name 'MyShare' -AccountName 'DOMAIN\Sales' -AccessRight Change
Revoke-SmbShareAccess -Name 'MyShare' -AccountName 'DOMAIN\OldGroup'
Get-SmbShareAccess -Name 'MyShare'
```

### Best practice
Share = 'Everyone: Full Control' (permisivo). NTFS controlados granularmente.

Why: simplifica admin — solo mantenés NTFS.

## NTFS permissions

### Basic
- Full Control
- Modify
- Read & Execute
- List Folder Contents
- Read
- Write

### Advanced (32 specific rights)
- Traverse Folder
- List Folder
- Read Attributes
- Read Extended Attributes
- Create Files
- Create Folders
- Write Attributes
- Etc.

### Via GUI
Right-click → **Properties → Security → Edit**.

### Via PowerShell
```powershell
$acl = Get-Acl 'D:\Shares\Sales'
$rule = New-Object System.Security.AccessControl.FileSystemAccessRule(
    'DOMAIN\Sales', 
    'Modify', 
    'ContainerInherit,ObjectInherit', 
    'None', 
    'Allow'
)
$acl.SetAccessRule($rule)
Set-Acl 'D:\Shares\Sales' $acl
```

### Via icacls (comando CLI)
```powershell
icacls 'D:\Shares\Sales' /grant 'DOMAIN\Sales:(OI)(CI)M'
icacls 'D:\Shares\Sales' /remove 'DOMAIN\OldGroup'
icacls 'D:\Shares\Sales'   # Ver current permissions
```

Flags:
- **OI** = Object Inherit (files inherit)
- **CI** = Container Inherit (subfolders inherit)
- **IO** = Inherit Only (no aplica al object mismo)

Permissions:
- **F** — Full Control
- **M** — Modify
- **RX** — Read + Execute
- **R** — Read
- **W** — Write

## Inheritance
NTFS permissions inherit desde parent folder por default.

### Break inheritance
```powershell
$acl = Get-Acl 'D:\Shares\Sensitive'
$acl.SetAccessRuleProtection($true, $false)   # $true = protected, $false = don't copy inherited
Set-Acl 'D:\Shares\Sensitive' $acl
```

En UI: Properties → Security → Advanced → Disable inheritance.

### Restore inheritance
```powershell
$acl.SetAccessRuleProtection($false, $false)
```

## Groups vs users

### Best practice: AGDLP
- **A**ccount → **G**lobal group → **D**omain **L**ocal group → **P**ermission

Ejemplo:
1. Users (accounts): jperez, mgomez
2. Global group: G_Sales_EU (contains users)
3. Domain Local group: DL_Sales_Modify
4. Add G_Sales_EU to DL_Sales_Modify
5. Grant DL_Sales_Modify Modify NTFS en folder

Beneficio: para nuevos users → add al global group. No touch permissions.

## Ownership

### Ver
```powershell
(Get-Acl 'D:\Shares\Sales').Owner
```

### Change
```powershell
$acl = Get-Acl 'D:\Shares\Sales'
$acl.SetOwner([System.Security.Principal.NTAccount]'DOMAIN\Admin')
Set-Acl 'D:\Shares\Sales' $acl
```

Or:
```powershell
takeown /f 'D:\Shares\Sales' /r /d y
```

## Effective Access
Combina all group memberships:

### GUI
Properties → Security → Advanced → **Effective Access** tab → select user → see actual rights.

### PowerShell
```powershell
# Not built-in cmdlet — check membership manually
Get-ADPrincipalGroupMembership jperez
```

Contrast con groups en ACL → determine access.

## Auditing
Log file access:

### Enable object access auditing
**GPO**: Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security → Advanced Audit Policy Configuration → Object Access:
- Audit File System: Success + Failure

### Enable per-folder audit
Properties → Security → Advanced → **Auditing** tab → Add:
- User: Everyone
- Access: Read, Write, Delete
- Type: All

Events log en Security event log (Event ID 4663).

Filter en SIEM o Event Viewer.

## Common patterns

### Read-only para users, RW para admins
- Users NTFS: Read
- Admins NTFS: Modify

### Deny
Denies win over allows. Use sparingly (confuse admins).

### Access-Based Enumeration (ABE)
Hide subfolders users can't access:
```powershell
Set-SmbShare -Name 'MyShare' -FolderEnumerationMode AccessBased
```

User browse share → solo ve folders donde tiene at least Read.

## Troubleshooting

### 'Access denied' aunque tenga permisos
- New group membership? Requires logoff/logon (Kerberos ticket refresh)
- Deny en algún lugar
- Share permissions más restrictivas que NTFS

### Ver membresías del user
```powershell
Get-ADPrincipalGroupMembership jperez | Select Name
```

### Ver permissions efectivas
```powershell
(Get-Acl 'D:\Shares\Sales').Access | Format-Table IdentityReference, FileSystemRights, AccessControlType
```

### Whoami
```powershell
whoami /groups
```

Muestra all groups en current session.

## Bulk operations

### Reset all permissions en tree
```powershell
icacls 'D:\Shares\Sales' /reset /t /c
```

Careful — removes non-inherited rules.

### Copy permissions
```powershell
$acl = Get-Acl 'D:\Shares\Source'
Set-Acl 'D:\Shares\Destination' $acl
```

### Add group a muchas folders
```powershell
Get-ChildItem 'D:\Shares\Sales' -Directory -Recurse | ForEach {
    $acl = Get-Acl $_.FullName
    $rule = New-Object System.Security.AccessControl.FileSystemAccessRule(
        'DOMAIN\Auditors', 'Read', 'ContainerInherit,ObjectInherit', 'None', 'Allow')
    $acl.AddAccessRule($rule)
    Set-Acl $_.FullName $acl
}
```

## SDDL (Security Descriptor Definition Language)
String representation of ACL:
```
O:BAG:BAD:(A;OICI;FA;;;BA)(A;OICI;0x1200a9;;;S-1-5-32-545)
```

### Get SDDL
```powershell
(Get-Acl 'D:\Shares\Sales').Sddl
```

### Set SDDL
```powershell
$acl = Get-Acl 'D:\Shares\Sales'
$acl.SetSecurityDescriptorSddlForm($sddl)
Set-Acl 'D:\Shares\Sales' $acl
```

Útil para portability + audit.

## Encryption (EFS)
### Encrypt file
```powershell
cipher /e /a 'D:\Sensitive\file.txt'
```

Solo el user que cifró (o Data Recovery Agent) puede abrir.

### Certificate needed
User needs EFS certificate. Auto-created on first encrypt.

### Backup EFS cert
Critical — sin cert, data no recoverable.

## Common issues

### 'Cannot change permissions'
- Not owner
- Take ownership first (`takeown`)

### 'Slow con many files'
- Millions de files con custom ACLs — inheritance más eficiente
- Use groups (fewer ACL entries)

### 'ACL grew unbounded'
- Direct user permissions accumulated
- Refactor con groups

## Best practices
- **AGDLP model** — groups over individual users
- **Simple share permissions** (Everyone Full Control) + strict NTFS
- **Inheritance por default** — break only para specific cases
- **Document ownership + auditors**
- **ABE enabled** — reduce info leakage
- **Regular access review** — quién accede qué
- **Audit sensitive folders** — quién leyó/modificó

## Autorización
- Local admin (server) para change permissions
- Ownership permission required para some operations
- Delegated via Restricted Groups en GPO

title: Windows Server: WMI + PSRemoting para admin remoto
tags: wmi, wmic, psremoting, winrm, remote admin
excerpt: Administración remota con WMI y PowerShell Remoting.
body:
## WMI (Windows Management Instrumentation)
API + database de management info:
- OS state
- Hardware
- Software
- Services
- Events

## Consultar WMI

### PowerShell (moderno — CIM)
```powershell
Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select Version, Caption
Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem | Select Manufacturer, Model, TotalPhysicalMemory
Get-CimInstance Win32_LogicalDisk | Select DeviceID, Size, FreeSpace
Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Where State -eq Running | Select Name, StartMode
Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Sort WorkingSetSize -Desc | Select -First 10
Get-CimInstance Win32_NetworkAdapterConfiguration | Where IPEnabled -eq true | Select IPAddress
```

### PowerShell (legacy — WMI)
```powershell
Get-WmiObject Win32_OperatingSystem
```

Modern: prefer `Get-CimInstance` (WMI protocol, no DCOM issues).

### wmic (CLI legacy — deprecated)
```powershell
wmic os get Caption, Version
wmic logicaldisk get DeviceID, Size, FreeSpace
wmic process list brief
```

SAP prefer PowerShell now.

## WMI classes populares
- `Win32_OperatingSystem`
- `Win32_ComputerSystem`
- `Win32_Processor`
- `Win32_LogicalDisk`
- `Win32_PhysicalMemory`
- `Win32_NetworkAdapterConfiguration`
- `Win32_Service`
- `Win32_Process`
- `Win32_UserAccount`
- `Win32_Group`
- `Win32_ProductInstalled` (software)
- `Win32_QuickFixEngineering` (patches)

## Remoto

### CIM (recomendado)
```powershell
Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem -ComputerName server01, server02, server03
```

Con credentials:
```powershell
$cred = Get-Credential
New-CimSession -ComputerName server01 -Credential $cred
```

### Batch con multiple servers
```powershell
$servers = 'server01', 'server02', 'server03'

Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_OperatingSystem -ComputerName $servers |
    Select PSComputerName, Caption, Version, LastBootUpTime
```

## PowerShell Remoting (WinRM)

### Enable
En target servers:
```powershell
Enable-PSRemoting -Force
```

Hace:
- Start WinRM service
- Firewall rule allow WinRM (5985 HTTP, 5986 HTTPS)
- Register PowerShell session configurations

### Ejecutar comando remoto
```powershell
Invoke-Command -ComputerName server01 -ScriptBlock { 
    Get-Service | Where Status -eq Running
}

# Multiple servers en paralelo
Invoke-Command -ComputerName server01, server02, server03 -ScriptBlock {
    Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem | Select TotalPhysicalMemory
}
```

### Con credentials
```powershell
$cred = Get-Credential
Invoke-Command -ComputerName server01 -Credential $cred -ScriptBlock { ... }
```

### Interactive session
```powershell
Enter-PSSession -ComputerName server01

# Ahora estás en el server remoto:
[server01]: PS> Get-Service
[server01]: PS> Exit-PSSession
```

### Persistent sessions
```powershell
$session = New-PSSession -ComputerName server01

Invoke-Command -Session $session -ScriptBlock { $global:counter = 100 }
Invoke-Command -Session $session -ScriptBlock { $global:counter }   # 100 (state persist)

Remove-PSSession $session
```

### Copy files
```powershell
Copy-Item -Path C:\local.txt -Destination C:\remote.txt -ToSession $session
Copy-Item -Path C:\remote.log -Destination C:\local.log -FromSession $session
```

## HTTPS PSRemoting
Para production, encrypt over HTTPS:

### En server target
```powershell
# Create cert (o import cert enterprise)
$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate -DnsName server01.empresa.local -CertStoreLocation cert:\LocalMachine\My

# Config listener HTTPS
New-Item -Path WSMan:\localhost\Listener -Transport HTTPS -Address * -CertificateThumbPrint $cert.Thumbprint -Force

# Firewall
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'WinRM HTTPS' -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 5986 -Action Allow
```

### Cliente conecta
```powershell
Invoke-Command -ComputerName server01 -UseSSL -ScriptBlock { ... }
```

## Trusted hosts (workgroup / cross-domain)
Si no en same domain, need trusted hosts:
```powershell
Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\TrustedHosts -Value 'server01,server02' -Force
```

Or specific range:
```powershell
Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\TrustedHosts -Value '*.empresa.local'
```

## JEA (Just Enough Administration)
Restrictive delegation:
- User can only run specific cmdlets
- Even if not admin
- Session config restricts what's exposed

### Ejemplo
```powershell
# Session configuration
$config = @{
    SessionType = 'RestrictedRemoteServer'
    VisibleCmdlets = 'Get-Service', 'Restart-Service'
    RoleDefinitions = @{
        'DOMAIN\Help Desk' = @{ RoleCapabilities = 'ServiceOps' }
    }
}

New-PSSessionConfigurationFile -Path C:\JEA\ServiceMgmt.pssc @config
Register-PSSessionConfiguration -Name ServiceOps -Path C:\JEA\ServiceMgmt.pssc
```

Users connect a config `ServiceOps` → solo pueden ejecutar Get-Service + Restart-Service.

## Common issues

### 'Access is denied'
- User no en Administrators group del target
- No en Remote Management Users group
- WinRM listener no activo

### 'The client cannot connect to the destination'
- WinRM service stopped en target
- Firewall blocking 5985/5986
- Trusted hosts config wrong

### 'Kerberos error'
- Time skew > 5 min
- SPN missing
- Cross-domain trust issue

### 'Timeout'
- Slow network
- Long-running command
- Increase: `Invoke-Command -SessionOption (New-PSSessionOption -OperationTimeout 300000)`

### 'Language mode restricted'
- JEA o Constrained Language enabled
- Some cmdlets blocked

## Best practices

### 1. HTTPS PSRemoting en production
HTTP OK en labs, no producción.

### 2. JEA para delegación
Operators solo lo que necesitan.

### 3. Config baseline
Standard PSRemoting config en all servers via GPO / DSC.

### 4. Log everything
Record all remote sessions:
```powershell
$PSDefaultParameterValues['Invoke-Command:LogPipelineExecutionDetails'] = $true
```

### 5. Audit script blocks
GPO: enable PowerShell script block logging.

### 6. Use CIM sessions
Más moderno, menos overhead:
```powershell
$session = New-CimSession -ComputerName server01
Get-CimInstance -CimSession $session Win32_OperatingSystem
```

### 7. Bulk operations
```powershell
$servers | ForEach-Object -Parallel {
    Invoke-Command -ComputerName $_ -ScriptBlock { ... }
} -ThrottleLimit 10
```

PowerShell 7 parallel jobs.

## Alternativas cloud-native
- **Azure Automation** — runbooks cloud-based
- **Ansible Windows modules** — via WinRM
- **Chef / Puppet** — full config management
- **Intune** — device management + scripts

## Autorización
- Local Administrators (o Remote Management Users)
- JEA para restricted access
- Delegated via GPO

## Common WMI queries

### Uptime
```powershell
(Get-Date) - (Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).LastBootUpTime
```

### Installed software
```powershell
Get-CimInstance Win32_Product | Select Name, Version, InstallDate
```

(Lento — usa registry query alternative para speed).

### Patches installed
```powershell
Get-CimInstance Win32_QuickFixEngineering | Sort InstalledOn -Desc
```

### Disk usage
```powershell
Get-CimInstance Win32_LogicalDisk | ForEach {
    [PSCustomObject]@{
        Drive = $_.DeviceID
        SizeGB = [math]::Round($_.Size / 1GB, 2)
        FreeGB = [math]::Round($_.FreeSpace / 1GB, 2)
        PctFree = [math]::Round($_.FreeSpace / $_.Size * 100, 2)
    }
}
```

### Running services
```powershell
Get-Service | Where Status -eq Running | Select Name, DisplayName
```

### Top processes por memoria
```powershell
Get-Process | Sort WorkingSet -Desc | Select -First 10 Name, WorkingSet, CPU
```

title: Windows Server: performance monitoring + baselining
tags: perfmon, performance, counter, baseline, windows server
excerpt: Monitor performance de Windows Server + establecer baselines.
body:
## Performance Monitor (perfmon)

### Ejecutar
`perfmon.exe`

### Vistas
- **Performance Monitor** — real-time charts
- **Data Collector Sets** — recording sessions
- **Reports** — analyze recordings

## Core counters

### CPU
- `\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time` — total CPU used
- `\Processor(*)\% Processor Time` — per core
- `\System\Processor Queue Length` — >2 per core = CPU bottleneck
- `\Process(*)\% Processor Time` — per process

### Memory
- `\Memory\Available MBytes` — RAM disponible
- `\Memory\Pages/sec` — paging activity
- `\Memory\Committed Bytes` — total memory committed
- `\Memory\Pool Nonpaged Bytes` — kernel memory (grows con handles)
- `\Memory\Pool Paged Bytes`
- `\Paging File(_Total)\% Usage` — pagefile use

### Disk
- `\PhysicalDisk(*)\Avg. Disk Queue Length` — >2 = bottleneck
- `\PhysicalDisk(*)\% Idle Time` — inverse of busy
- `\PhysicalDisk(*)\Avg. Disk sec/Read` — latency <20ms healthy
- `\PhysicalDisk(*)\Avg. Disk sec/Write`
- `\LogicalDisk(*)\% Free Space`

### Network
- `\Network Interface(*)\Bytes Total/sec`
- `\Network Interface(*)\Current Bandwidth`
- `\Network Interface(*)\Output Queue Length` — >2 = saturation
- `\TCPv4\Segments Retransmitted/sec` — network issues

### System
- `\System\System Up Time`
- `\System\Context Switches/sec` — >30k = overhead
- `\System\File Read Bytes/sec`

## Data Collector Sets

### Create
1. Data Collector Sets → **User Defined** → right-click → **New → Data Collector Set**
2. Name: `Baseline_2026-Q3`
3. Choose 'Create manually (Advanced)'
4. Add counters
5. Schedule (start/stop times, days)
6. Location (log file path)

### Format
- **BLG (binary)** — best for large datasets
- **CSV** — Excel-friendly
- **TSV**
- **SQL** — write to DB

### Sample interval
- 15 sec (default) — good para most cases
- 1 sec — troubleshooting spikes
- 60+ sec — long-term trending

## Baselining
Record normal behavior:
- 1-week baseline durante business ops
- Contains: CPU, memory, disk, network avg + peaks
- Save archived

### Cuando compare
- After change (software install, config)
- Complaints of slowness
- Capacity planning

## typeperf (CLI)
```powershell
# Sample counter 10 times, 1 sec interval
typeperf '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time' -sc 10

# Multiple counters + save to CSV
typeperf ^
    '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time' ^
    '\Memory\Available MBytes' ^
    '\PhysicalDisk(_Total)\Avg. Disk Queue Length' ^
    -si 5 -sc 60 -f CSV -o C:\perf.csv
```

Útil para automatización + scripts.

## logman (CLI para data collector sets)
```powershell
# Create
logman create counter Baseline -cf counters.cfg -si 30 -f bincirc -max 100 -o C:\perflogs\baseline

# Start
logman start Baseline

# Query
logman query Baseline

# Stop
logman stop Baseline
```

## Análisis

### PAL (Performance Analysis of Logs)
Herramienta gratis Microsoft (https://github.com/clinthuffman/PAL):
- Analyzes BLG files
- Compares con thresholds (SQL Server, IIS, general Windows)
- Genera HTML report con findings

### Excel
Open CSV → charts → identify patterns.

### Custom scripts
Parse CSV con PowerShell:
```powershell
$data = Import-Csv C:\perf.csv
$data | Where { [double]$_.'\\SERVER01\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time' -gt 80 } |
    Select 'Time', '\\SERVER01\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time'
```

See moments of high CPU.

## Real-time performance con Task Manager

### Improved perf tab (Windows Server 2019+)
- **Performance** tab shows CPU, memory, disk, network graphs
- Per-process breakdown en **Details** tab
- **Users** tab per-user resource usage

### Resource Monitor (`resmon.exe`)
Deep dive:
- Overview, CPU, Memory, Disk, Network
- Per-process file handles, network connections
- Show which files están locked por which process

## Event Tracing for Windows (ETW)
Lightweight profiling framework.

### PerfView (Microsoft, free)
GUI para ETW:
- Analyze CPU stacks
- Find memory leaks
- Trace network events
- .NET-specific analysis

Gratis download.

### xperf
CLI de Windows Performance Toolkit:
```powershell
xperf -on Base -stackwalk profile
# Reproducir problem
xperf -stop -d trace.etl
xperfview trace.etl
```

## Windows Performance Recorder / Analyzer (WPR/WPA)
Modern replacement de xperf:
- Record: `wpr -start GeneralProfile`
- Stop: `wpr -stop trace.etl`
- Analyze: `WPA.exe trace.etl`

## Alerts

### Perfmon alert
Data Collector Set con action:
- If counter > threshold → log entry + trigger task

### Config
1. Data Collector Sets → new → 'Create Manually'
2. Type: **Performance Counter Alert**
3. Add counter + threshold (ej: `\Memory\Available MBytes < 500`)
4. Alert action: run task (script)

### PowerShell script alert
```powershell
$avail = (Get-Counter '\Memory\Available MBytes').CounterSamples.CookedValue

if ($avail -lt 500) {
    Send-MailMessage -To admin@empresa.com -From alerts@empresa.com -Subject 'Low memory' -Body "Server $env:COMPUTERNAME has only $avail MB free"
}
```

Schedule con Task Scheduler.

## Third-party tools
- **PRTG** — enterprise monitoring
- **Zabbix** (con Windows agent)
- **Datadog**, **New Relic** — cloud
- **Splunk Universal Forwarder** — logs + metrics a SIEM

## Common issues + counters

### App slow
- CPU: `% Processor Time` — if consistently >80%
- Memory: `Available MBytes` — if <500
- Disk: `Avg. Disk sec/Read` — if >20ms
- Network: `Bytes Total/sec` — near NIC max

### Memory leak
- `Process\Private Bytes` (per process) — growing continuamente
- `Memory\Pool Nonpaged Bytes` — kernel-level leak

### Disk bottleneck
- `Avg. Disk Queue Length > 2`
- `% Idle Time < 20%`
- Solutions: faster disks, add spindles, optimize queries

### High context switching
- `System\Context Switches/sec > 30000`
- Symptom of thread contention
- Reduce concurrent threads o optimize code

## Best practices
- **Baseline first** — sin baseline no sabes qué es 'normal'
- **Regular sampling** — weekly baselines
- **Store historical** — trend analysis
- **Focus critical counters** — don't collect everything
- **Correlate con events** — logs, apps, users
- **Automated alerts** — critical thresholds
- **Document normal** — establish ranges per counter per server

## Autorización
- Local admin para install counters
- Members del **Performance Log Users** group para collect data
- Members del **Performance Monitor Users** para read

title: Windows Server: certificados con AD CS (Enterprise CA)
tags: ad cs, certificate authority, pki, windows server
excerpt: Setup + operar Enterprise CA con Active Directory Certificate Services.
body:
## AD CS
Active Directory Certificate Services — PKI integrated con AD:
- Issue certificates para users, computers, servers
- Auto-enrollment via GPO
- CRL + OCSP
- Cert templates customizables

## Install
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature ADCS-Cert-Authority -IncludeManagementTools
```

## Post-install config
```powershell
Install-AdcsCertificationAuthority \
    -CAType EnterpriseRootCA \
    -CryptoProviderName 'RSA#Microsoft Software Key Storage Provider' \
    -KeyLength 4096 \
    -HashAlgorithmName SHA256 \
    -CACommonName 'Empresa Root CA' \
    -CADistinguishedNameSuffix 'DC=empresa,DC=local' \
    -ValidityPeriod Years \
    -ValidityPeriodUnits 10
```

### CA Types
- **EnterpriseRootCA** — integrated con AD (recomendado)
- **EnterpriseSubordinateCA** — child de otro CA
- **StandaloneRootCA** — offline CA (best security para root)
- **StandaloneSubordinateCA**

### Enterprise recommended structure
```
Offline Root CA (Standalone, air-gapped)
    └─ Issuing CA (Enterprise Subordinate)
           └─ Certificates emitidos
```

Offline root minimiza risk. Issuing CA es lo que day-to-day emite certs.

## Certificate templates

### View templates
`Certification Authority` (`certsrv.msc`) → Certificate Templates → **Manage** (opens `certtmpl.msc`).

### Duplicate existing
1. Right-click 'User' template → **Duplicate Template**
2. Modify:
   - **Compatibility** — target Windows version
   - **General**:
     - Display name: 'ZUser'
     - Validity: 1 year (default 2)
     - Renewal: 6 weeks before expiry
   - **Cryptography**:
     - RSA 2048 minimum
     - CSP: Microsoft Software Key Storage Provider
   - **Subject Name**:
     - Build from AD info: ✓
     - Include email: ✓
   - **Security**:
     - Domain Users: Read + Enroll + Autoenroll

### Publish template
`certsrv.msc` → Certificate Templates → **New → Certificate Template to Issue** → seleccionar 'ZUser'.

## Auto-enrollment

### GPO Computer
Computer Config → Policies → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Public Key Policies:
- **Certificate Services Client - Auto-Enrollment**:
  - Enabled
  - ✓ Renew expired certs
  - ✓ Update certs that use templates

### GPO User
Mismo path but User Config.

### Trigger
```powershell
certutil -pulse
# Force auto-enrollment check
```

O users get certs at next login.

## Ver certs enrolled
### Machine
```powershell
Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My
```

### User
```powershell
Get-ChildItem Cert:\CurrentUser\My
```

### GUI
`certlm.msc` (Local Machine) o `certmgr.msc` (Current User).

## Common cert types

### Server Authentication
Use for HTTPS websites, RDP, LDAPS.

Subject Alternative Name (SAN) con FQDNs:
- CN: `sap.empresa.local`
- SAN: `sap.empresa.local, sap-alt.empresa.local`

### Client Authentication
For VPN, wireless, mTLS.

### Code Signing
For signing scripts, executables, drivers.

### EFS (Encrypting File System)
Users encrypt files.

### Smart Card Logon
MFA con smart cards.

## Request cert manually

### GUI
`certlm.msc` → **Personal → Certificates** → right-click → **All Tasks → Request New Certificate**.

Wizard:
1. Select policy (Active Directory Enrollment Policy)
2. Select template
3. Provide details (SAN, contact info)
4. Enroll

### CLI
```powershell
# Info file
$inf = @'
[Version]
Signature='$Windows NT$'

[NewRequest]
Subject = 'CN=sap.empresa.local'
KeyLength = 2048
KeySpec = 1
MachineKeySet = TRUE
Exportable = FALSE
RequestType = PKCS10

[Extensions]
2.5.29.17 = '{text}dns=sap.empresa.local&dns=sap-alt.empresa.local'
'@

$inf | Out-File C:\request.inf
certreq -new C:\request.inf C:\request.req
certreq -submit -config 'CA-Server\Empresa CA' C:\request.req C:\cert.cer
certreq -accept C:\cert.cer
```

## OCSP (Online Certificate Status Protocol)
Faster que CRL — real-time lookups:

### Install responder
```powershell
Install-WindowsFeature ADCS-Online-Cert -IncludeManagementTools
Install-AdcsOnlineResponder -CAConfig 'CA-Server\Empresa CA' -Confirm:$false
```

### Config revocation configuration
`Online Responder Management Console` → **Revocation Configuration** → **Add**:
- Name: 'Empresa CA OCSP'
- Bind to issuing CA

### Client uses
Certs contain URL to OCSP responder. Client queries → verifies not revoked.

## CRL (Certificate Revocation List)
Legacy method. File con lista de revoked certs.

### Publish
```powershell
certutil -crl
```

Generado en `C:\Windows\System32\CertSrv\CertEnroll\<CA>.crl`.

### Distribute via HTTP
Publish CRL Distribution Points (CDPs):
- `http://ca-server.empresa.local/certdata/EmpresaCA.crl`

IIS site hosts these.

## Revoke cert
```powershell
certutil -revoke <serial-number>
```

GUI: `certsrv.msc` → **Issued Certificates** → right-click → **Revoke**.

Reason codes:
- KeyCompromise
- CACompromise
- AffiliationChanged
- Superseded
- CessationOfOperation

## Backup CA

### PowerShell
```powershell
Backup-CARoleService -Path 'C:\CA-Backup' -Password (ConvertTo-SecureString 'BackupPass' -AsPlainText -Force)
```

Includes private key + database.

**Almacenar offline, encrypted.** Loss of CA private key = disaster.

### Restore
```powershell
Restore-CARoleService -Path 'C:\CA-Backup' -Password ...
```

## Renew CA cert
Antes de expiry (10 años default), renew:

1. `certsrv.msc` → right-click CA → **All Tasks → Renew CA Certificate**
2. Reuse existing key or generate new
3. New cert issued (still valid for existing certs signed antes)

## Common issues

### 'Auto-enrollment no funciona'
- GPO not applied — `gpresult /r`
- Template permissions wrong (Autoenroll not granted)
- CA not published en AD (verify `certsrv.msc`)
- Client can't reach CA (firewall / DNS)

### 'Cert expired mid-lifecycle'
- Auto-renewal should catch — check GPO
- Renewal threshold in template config

### 'CRL check failed'
- CRL URL unreachable
- CRL expired (CA not publishing new)
- Force publish: `certutil -crl`

### 'Cert chain untrusted'
- Root CA not en trust store of client
- Enterprise CAs auto-added via AD, but non-domain clients need manual import

## Best practices

### 1. Offline Root CA
Root CA en air-gapped machine (VM shut down, offline). Turn on solo para renew issuing CA cert (once every 5 years).

### 2. Issuing CA online
Day-to-day cert issuance. Multiple para HA if needed.

### 3. Cert templates well-designed
Specific templates per use case. Don't reuse 'User' template for everything.

### 4. Auto-enrollment
Users + servers get certs sin manual intervention.

### 5. Monitor cert expiry
```powershell
Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where NotAfter -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(30) |
    Select Subject, NotAfter, Thumbprint
```

Alert cuando <30 days remaining.

### 6. Backup regular
Weekly backup del CA DB.

### 7. OCSP for revocation
Faster than CRL, mejor UX.

### 8. Compliance documented
CA cert lifecycle documented para audits.

## Autorización
- Enterprise Admins para install CA
- CA Administrators para issue/revoke certs
- Certificate Managers para template management
- Auditors — read-only

## Migration to newer version
AD CS backwards compatible. Migrating CA server:
1. Backup old CA
2. Install new server con AD CS
3. Restore backup on new
4. Update DNS/host records
5. Old server decommission después de verify

title: Windows Server: task scheduler para automation
tags: task scheduler, automation, schtasks, scheduled task
body:
## Task Scheduler
Windows built-in scheduler para run programs/scripts en times/events específicos.

### Ubicación
- `taskschd.msc` (GUI)
- `schtasks` (legacy CLI)
- `Get-ScheduledTask` / `Register-ScheduledTask` (PowerShell moderno)

## Basic scheduled task

### PowerShell
```powershell
# Action: qué ejecutar
$action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'PowerShell.exe' -Argument '-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\Scripts\backup.ps1'

# Trigger: cuándo
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 3AM

# Principal: como qué user
$principal = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId 'SYSTEM' -LogonType ServiceAccount -RunLevel Highest

# Settings
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries -StartWhenAvailable

# Register
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'DailyBackup' -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Principal $principal -Settings $settings
```

### GUI
1. `taskschd.msc`
2. **Create Task**
3. Tabs:
   - **General** — name, user, run level
   - **Triggers** — when
   - **Actions** — what
   - **Conditions** — network, idle, power
   - **Settings** — retry, delete after, etc.

## Triggers avanzados

### On event
Dispara cuando aparece un event específico en Event Log:
```powershell
$class = 'System'
$id = 6008   # unexpected shutdown

$trigger = New-CimInstance -CimClass (Get-CimClass -ClassName MSFT_TaskEventTrigger -Namespace ROOT\Microsoft\Windows\TaskScheduler) -ClientOnly
$trigger.Subscription = @"
<QueryList>
    <Query Id='0' Path='$class'>
        <Select Path='$class'>*[System[(EventID=$id)]]</Select>
    </Query>
</QueryList>
"@
$trigger.Enabled = $true

Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'AlertUnexpectedShutdown' -Trigger $trigger -Action $action -RunLevel Highest -User 'SYSTEM'
```

Event 6008 (unexpected shutdown) → execute alert script.

### On idle
```powershell
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -RunOnlyIfIdle -IdleDuration (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 10)
```

Runs only if PC idle 10+ min.

### At workstation lock/unlock
```powershell
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogOn
# Or event ID 4800 (workstation lock)
```

### Multiple triggers
```powershell
$t1 = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 3AM
$t2 = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtStartup
$t3 = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogOn

Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'MultipleTriggers' -Trigger $t1, $t2, $t3 -Action $action
```

### Repeat interval
```powershell
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At (Get-Date) -RepetitionInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 15) -RepetitionDuration (New-TimeSpan -Days 365)
```

Every 15 min forever.

## Actions múltiples
```powershell
$a1 = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'cmd.exe' -Argument '/c net stop miServicio'
```

## Conditions

### Network required
```powershell
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -RunOnlyIfNetworkAvailable
```

### Battery
```powershell
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries:$false -AllowStartIfOnBatteries:$false
```

No runs si laptop en battery.

### Wake computer
```powershell
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -WakeToRun
```

PC wakes from sleep para ejecutar.

## Principal (user context)

### Local SYSTEM
Runs con highest privileges:
```powershell
$principal = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId 'SYSTEM' -LogonType ServiceAccount -RunLevel Highest
```

### Domain service account
Better para audit + rotation:
```powershell
$principal = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId 'DOMAIN\svc_backup' -LogonType Password -RunLevel Highest

Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Backup' -Principal $principal -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Password (Read-Host -AsSecureString 'Password')
```

Requires password (secure storage).

### gMSA (Group Managed Service Account)
Best — no password management:
```powershell
$principal = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId 'DOMAIN\gmsa_backup$' -LogonType Password -RunLevel Highest

Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Backup' -Principal $principal -Action $action -Trigger $trigger
# No password required — Windows manages
```

### Configure for run whether logged on or not
```powershell
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName '...' -RunLevel Highest -LogonType S4U  # sin password required, cred cached
```

## Task retention

### Delete after
```powershell
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -DeleteExpiredTaskAfter (New-TimeSpan -Days 30)
```

### Ver ran history
```powershell
Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName 'DailyBackup'
# LastRunTime, LastTaskResult (0 = success), NextRunTime
```

### Task result codes
- `0` — success
- `0x1` — general error
- `0x41306` — task terminated por user
- `0x41303` — task never run
- `0x8007xxxx` — Windows error

## Common issues

### 'Task shows Result 0x1'
Generic error. Debug:
- Log output al file: `-Argument '-File script.ps1 *>&1 | Out-File C:\logs\task.log'`
- Check event log Task Scheduler (`Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational`)

### 'Task not running at scheduled time'
- Machine off/sleeping
- User no logged (if RunOnlyIfLoggedOn)
- Network condition fails

### 'Task runs but nothing happens'
- Script running but errors internally
- Check script logging
- Interactive commands (prompts) hang forever — never interactive en scheduled tasks

### 'Access denied'
- Task runs as wrong user
- Script has permission issues
- File paths unreadable

## Best practices

### 1. Logging
Scripts should log to file (never silent):
```powershell
Start-Transcript -Path 'C:\Logs\backup-$(Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd).log'
# script content
Stop-Transcript
```

### 2. Error handling
Exit codes matter:
```powershell
try {
    # main work
    exit 0
} catch {
    Write-Error $_
    exit 1
}
```

### 3. Idempotency
Safe to run multiple times. Check state antes de action.

### 4. Documentation
Comment task purpose en description field.

### 5. Naming convention
`<Team>_<Purpose>_<Frequency>` — ej: `IT_Backup_Daily`, `HR_UserSync_Hourly`.

### 6. Central location scripts
`C:\Scripts\` or network share. Backup regularly.

### 7. gMSA over user accounts
No password rotation issues.

### 8. Monitoring
Alert cuando `LastTaskResult != 0`.
